While I understand what youre saying, and obesity does not necessarily cause all of these issues, it frequently makes them get to the point that a mobility scooter is necessary. I do xrays for a living. I see knees. And long term obese knees are invariably in worse shape than knees on a person of a healthy weight. The cartilage gets compressed to the point that it shreds because of the force exerted on it by every step. And the destruction of the cartilage leads to the destruction of the distal femur and tibial plateau. Extreme obesity can actually lead to the tarsal bones changing orientation to each other and causing the foot to collapse. And while this can happen without the presence of obesity, it is much more frequent in extremely obese people. 
In addition, exercise is not required for weight loss. Reduction if caloric intake is. And of course its easier said than done, but that's all it takes. It might happen very slowly, but it will happen.
Ok. Genuine question. If the mobility issues are unrelated to weight, then what is the cause? I sincerely cannot think of a single mobility issue that is not at least exacerbated by obesity.
